newsitem.title: USA: Grossberg interview violates gag order-prosecutors.
newsitem.headline: Grossberg interview violates gag order-prosecutors.

text.p: Prosecutors in the case of two New Jersey teenagers charged with killing their newborn son said on Monday that a court-imposed gag order was violated when the woman and her parents were interviewed by Barbara Walters on the ABC-TV show "20/20."

Amy Grossberg, 18, and her parents, Sonye and Alan Grossberg, were interviewed on Friday and the programme was aired on Sunday night. In court papers, prosecutors said the interviews violated a Nov. 21 order by Judge Henry duPont Ridgely limiting pre-trial publicity.
Grossberg and Brian Peterson Jr., 18, are charged with killing their infant immediately after his birth on Nov. 12 and dumping the body in a trash container.
The Delaware Attorney General's office filed a 70-page motion in Delaware Superior Court on Monday seeking sanctions against Grossberg and her attorney, Robert Gottlieb.
"Certain factual matters were misrepresented by the participants during the course of the television broadcast," court papers say.

Prosecutors said the "20/20" interview also violated a promise made by Grossberg's original team of lawyers, Charles Oberly III, Kathleen Jennings, and Charles Slanina. The prosecutors said that during a Jan. 15 teleconference, Grossberg's defence team said "We do not intend to go on any television shows (or) conduct any extensive interviews."
Slanina has already asked to withdraw from the case and on Monday, Oberly and Jennings filed a similar request. The "20/20" interview was arranged by Gottlieb who joined the defence team May 12.

Prosecutors asked Ridgely to find Gottlieb in contempt of the gag order, to disqualify him from further participation in the case, and to apply "appropriate" sanctions against Amy Grossberg. Peterson has not given any interviews to the media and is not part of the state's motion seeking sanctions.

After serving two months in Delaware prisons, the two teenagers were freed in January on $300,000 bail each and have been living in their respective homes in Wyckoff, New Jersey, under curfew and electronic monitoring.

The two were charged with delivering their infant son in a Newark, Delaware, motel, killing him and putting the body in a dumpster. At the time Peterson was a freshman at Gettysburg College in Pennsylvania and Grossberg was a freshman at the Unversity of Delaware in Newark.
Each faces charges of first-degree murder and murder by abuse or neglect. Potential sentences range from 15 years in prison to the death penalty. The trial is scheduled to begin Sept. 9.
